text:
ben_customer: Hey team, after upgrading to redwood-sdk==1.4.0 my app throws ImportError on startup. Worked on 1.3.x.

ben_customer: Error: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood.client'

alice_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste the pip/poetry output and your install command? also what python version and linux/darwin?

ben_customer: using poetry, python 3.11 on ubuntu 22.04. pyproject snippet: 
```
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.11"
redwood-sdk = {version = "^1.4.0", extras = ["http"]}
```

ben_customer: `poetry install` completes but import fails at runtime in our docker image.

alice_support: can you run `poetry run python -c "import pkgutil; print(list(pkgutil.iter_modules()))"` or `pip show redwood-sdk` inside the venv?

ben_customer: ran `poetry run pip show redwood-sdk` -> Version: 1.4.0, Location: /opt/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages

ben_customer: `ls /opt/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood*` shows `redwood-1.4.0.dist-info` only, no package dir.

alice_support: hmm that suggests the wheel might have been uploaded without package files (metadata-only) or poetry editable/lock mixup. did you build from source or pull from our index?

ben_customer: pulled from PyPI. `pip download redwood-sdk==1.4.0` gives a `.whl` that seems odd: filename `redwood_sdk-1.4.0-py3-none-any.whl` size 3.2 KB.

chris_sre: deploy-bot triggered: package-size anomaly +1. Looks like the wheel is tiny. tagging eng-runtime.

alice_support: thanks @chris_sre. @ben_customer can you try `pip install redwood-sdk==1.3.9 --force-reinstall` in your image to confirm downgrade works?

ben_customer: downgraded to 1.3.9 and import works. logs show package files present.

alice_support: ok that narrows to 1.4.0 packaging. could you share the wheel file (`pip download --no-deps redwood-sdk==1.4.0` and attach) — I'll escalate to product/packaging. In the meantime if you need a patch on CI, pin to 1.3.9.

ben_customer: attaching wheel to ticket (uploaded to support). thanks. we saw this hit CI and prod at ~02:14 UTC. broke a cron job doing embeddings -> retried several times and inflated billing. can support confirm if retries will be refunded?

alice_support: sorry about the billing impact. I filed a billing case with charge IDs and timestamps you provided. We'll request a one-time credit for retry-related overages. pls DM charge ids. :pray:

chris_sre: ENG-INC-674 linked — engineering confirmed a bad release artifact was uploaded to PyPI (empty package contents due to publish script bug). rollback in progress: 1.4.0 yanked from PyPI and 1.4.1 with proper wheel being published.

install-bot: PyPI: package redwood-sdk v1.4.0 yanked by publisher. New release 1.4.1 published.

ben_customer: confirmed `pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.1` pulled properly and package dir present. import fixed. thanks all.

alice_support: great — closing the loop: please keep 1.3.9 pinned in lockfiles if you want immediate stability, otherwise 1.4.1 is the fix. billing team will follow up via DM/email about credits. reach out if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:

ben_customer: appreciate the quick turnaround, esp for the billing help. saved our cron budget.

chris_sre: follow-up action: add CI check that validates wheel contents (ensure top-level package directories present) before publishing. assigned to eng-release.

alice_support: note for docs: add troubleshooting snippet for "wheel present but no package dir" with commands: `unzip -l <wheel>` `pip show -f redwood-sdk` `ls $(python -c "import site; print(site.getsitepackages()[0])") | grep redwood`.

ben_customer: added to our runbook too. thanks!
